{{Short description|American mathematician (1929–2026)}}
'''Theodore Seio Chihara''' (March 14, 1929 – February 11, 2026) was an American mathematician working on [[orthogonal polynomials]] who introduced [[Al-Salam–Chihara polynomials]], [[Brenke–Chihara polynomials]], and [[Chihara–Ismail polynomials]]. His brother was composer [[Paul Chihara]]. He earned his PhD from [[Purdue University]], where his thesis advisor was [[Arthur Rosenthal]].<ref name="mathproject">{{cite web |title=Theodore Seio Chihara |url=https://www.mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=16790 |website=Mathematics Genealogy Project |access-date=February 16, 2026}}</ref> Chihara died on February 11, 2026, at the age of 96.<ref>[https://www.dignitymemorial.com/obituaries/bellevue-wa/theodore-chihara-12747946 Theodore Seio Chihara] Dignity Memorial</ref>
